title: Heliotrope - Interop Playbook & Marketplace Listing Sync
summary: Kickoff to align on a technical playbook for Redwood marketplace listing + joint reference architecture. Focus areas: packaging (helm/chart + OCI), VPC and private deployment options, KMS/HSM compatibility, entitlements & metering, and an ops runbook for canary + rollback. Agreed to run a short validation pilot and exchange security docs; Helio wants clarified network egress, audit log retention, and license/usage billing model before legal OKs listing.
topics: Marketplace packaging strategy: container + helm chart + SaaS connector
Private deployment options: VPC peering, on-prem installer, and air-gapped concerns
KMS integration and key management (bring-your-own KMS/HSM flow)
Usage metering, billing hooks, and entitlements for Marketplace listing
Canary/rollout playbook, rollback triggers, and SLO verification steps
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-03-08 15:30 PDT | Duration: ~62m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Avery Chen, Samir Rao, Lena Martinez (Redwood) | Nora Patel, Marcus Lee, Imani Rivera, Evan Cho (Heliotrope)

00:00:03 - Avery Chen: great — thanks everyone for joining we got about an hour. quick agenda recap: packaging, security/KMS, networking, metering, and then a runbook for rollout. is that still good on your side nora?
00:00:12 - Nora Patel: yeah that works. ive got Marcus and Imani here to handle the infra and security questions; Evan will follow on product and billing.
00:00:21 - Samir Rao: perfect. one quick thing — we brought an engineering runbook that maps to the marketplace requirements. i can screen share after the initial q&a.
00:00:29 - Marcus Lee: cool, just call out up front we run a hybrid environment, mostly managed cloud but we have a small on prem footprint for latency sensitive customers. want to make sure the listing supports both.
00:00:42 - Avery Chen: yep, understood. Redwood supports three deployment modes — hosted, dedicated, private — and for marketplace we usually provide a container image + helm chart plus an optional private connector for on prem. question for you: do you expect customers to bring their own KMS?
00:00:59 - Imani Rivera: yes we do. for regulated customers we need BYOK and an HSM-backed key option, plus audit retention for 7 years. SOC2 is baseline but some want ISO27001 too.
00:01:12 - Samir Rao: okay, our private control plane has KMS integration for AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and a PKCS#11 HSM flow for on prem HSMs. small caveat: we need a short-lived credential exchange for certs; we can share the exact handshake in the security doc.
00:01:30 - Evan Cho: how does network egress look? a bunch of our compliance folks worry about outbound traffic from air-gapped installs.
00:01:37 - Lena Martinez: good question. for the air-gapped pattern we have an offline installer — it's a tarball containing OCI images and an optional license bundle. for telemetry we support a muted mode where metrics are stored locally and uploaded via a customer-controlled proxy. that pattern is documented but we need to confirm your acceptance tests.
00:01:58 - Nora Patel: that offline installer sounds promising. whats the size and cadence of updates typically?
00:02:05 - Samir Rao: releases are ~200–800MB compressed depending on model variants; security patches more frequent. cadence: monthly minor, quarterly major, with emergency patches as needed.
00:02:17 - Marcus Lee: for the helm chart, we need values to toggle features: enableTelemetry=false, useLocalKV=true, useExternalKMS=true, and an option for using a service account vs node-binding.
00:02:31 - Samir Rao: we can add those flags.
00:02:33 - (brief crosstalk)
00:03:10 - Imani Rivera: on audit logs retention, we need immutable logs for 7 years and proof of deletion when requested. can Redwood provide a compliance export and support auditing?
00:03:24 - Avery Chen: yes we can provide export APIs, and we have an append-only audit log with retention controls. full delete proof would be part of the on-prem operator — that needs a signed attestation from your side after we run the script.
00:03:38 - Nora Patel: we will need that in writing for legal.
00:03:42 - Avery Chen: noted, we'll attach it to the security package.
00:03:47 - Samir Rao: switching to marketplace-specifics: billing/entitlements. Helio — do you want per-seat licensing, per-token, or a hybrid?
00:03:57 - Evan Cho: our customers vary; enterprise customers prefer committed capacity with monthly billing; smaller companies like usage-based. For the marketplace listing, we want Redwood to surface both a metering hook for usage and an entitlement flag for reserved capacity.
00:04:17 - Lena Martinez: we have a metering endpoint that emits token counts and request classes; we can map those to a marketplace metering SKU. for committed capacity, our Dedicated offering attaches a license token that shows up in the metering payload.
00:04:30 - Marcus Lee: what's the latency overhead for the metering calls? we want synchronous calls not to add >5ms per request.
00:04:37 - Samir Rao: metering is async — we batch and push every 10s by default. the sync hook is only for entitlement checks which are cached locally so the per-request path is unaffected.
00:04:50 - (laughter)
00:04:55 - Nora Patel: ok good. what about the reference architecture doc — could we get a canonical diagram for marketplace listing?
00:05:02 - Avery Chen: yes, we'll produce a joint refarch that includes three modes: listed-hosted, listed-dedicated, and listed-private with an on-prem connector. it will call out networking, KMS flows, and canary rollback paths.
00:05:18 - Nora Patel: i'd like a section that maps our support matrix — e.g., which features are available in which mode.
00:05:24 - Lena Martinez: we'll add a capabilities matrix.
00:05:28 - Marcus Lee: about rollback triggers — what monitors do you recommend? token latency P95, error-rate spike >1%, and kv cache miss surge?
00:05:37 - Samir Rao: yep those are good. plus we use model-quality regression tests — small prompt sets we can run automatically in canary to detect hallucination rate increases.
00:05:49 - Evan Cho: can we automate that test harness inside the marketplace preflight?
00:05:53 - Samir Rao: absolutely, we can include a lightweight harness and an evaluation checklist.
00:05:58 - Imani Rivera: one more security question: do you support SSO/SAML for admin console and RBAC scoping per-tenant?
00:06:05 - Avery Chen: yes SAML/SCIM and role-based policies. we also support audit-forwarding to your SIEM.
00:06:13 - Nora Patel: great. right now legal also wants a sample data processing addendum and classifies model outputs as not PII by default; can we get that language?
00:06:23 - Avery Chen: we have a DPA template and a model usage clause; i'll have legal share a draft.
00:06:29 - (pause)
00:06:42 - Samir Rao: technical follow-ups: Marcus we need your test VPC for the pilot and the public key for your HSM so our PKCS#11 flow can be validated. also want the list of internal customer personas so we can tailor the operator values.
00:06:58 - Marcus Lee: i'll share a sandbox VPC and schedule network windows.
00:07:03 - Nora Patel: timeline question — how long until a listing is ready assuming security & pilot go well?
00:07:09 - Lena Martinez: typical is 6–8 weeks: 2 weeks to validate packaging and security, 2–3 weeks for pilot and networking, then listing prep and legal signoffs. if we hit blockers it can stretch.
00:07:23 - Evan Cho: that timeline would work; our launch target is end of Q2.
00:07:28 - Avery Chen: ok end of Q2 is feasible if pilot starts in 2 weeks.
00:07:33 - (wrap-up)
00:07:40 - Avery Chen: recap — we will: share security package + DPA draft; deliver a joint refarch doc and capabilities matrix; provide an offline installer and helm chart with requested flags; Redwood will receive sandbox VPC details and HSM pubkey; run a 2-week validation pilot; and then schedule a listing preflight.
00:07:58 - Nora Patel: thanks everyone.
00:08:02 - Meeting ends.

Notes on transcript quality: some words mis-transcribed (PKCS11 as P-K-C-S eleven, kubernets sometimes spelled), minor speaker attribution errors in first 2 minutes.
action_items: Marcus Lee - Share sandbox VPC peering details and HSM public key - due 2027-03-12
Avery Chen - Send Redwood security package + DPA draft and signed attestation template - due 2027-03-10
Samir Rao - Publish helm chart prototype and offline installer tarball (with flags) to shared drive - due 2027-03-15
Lena Martinez - Produce joint refarch diagram and capabilities matrix - due 2027-03-11
Nora Patel - Coordinate legal review and confirm launch target end-of-Q2 - due 2027-03-18
next_steps: Redwood to send security package and DPA
Heliotrope to provide sandbox networking and HSM key
Run 2-week validation pilot once infra in place
Schedule listing preflight meeting after pilot
